business.text: Booking Holdings runs Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, Kayak and OpenTable. It takes a commission or a merchant margin on hotel rooms, flights and rentals booked through its sites and apps, and is the largest online travel company in the world by bookings.

headline: Quality rank 13 of 150, score 86. Bucket: compounder. Price 195.13 USD on 2026-09-04. Forward P/E 15.8 vs own 4 year median 29.5 (-47%). EV/EBITDA 14.4. -12% from 52 week high, -14% from all time high. Next fiscal year EPS estimate moved +0.5% in 90 days. Short interest 2.8% of float. Next earnings 2026-10-27. guidance_diff.why: The last two 8-K Exhibit 99.1 press releases for this name have not been pulled from EDGAR, so there is no mechanical guidance diff. This is the free substitute for a transcript: it carries the guidance figures and none of the questions.
guidance_diff.caveat: Mechanical. Two press releases, sentences with a forward-looking word and a figure, matched on metric and period. It does not read tone, it cannot see a guide given without a number, and a filer that changes how it names a period between releases shows one lapsed and one introduced where a reader would see one reiterated. The verbatim sentence sits under every row so the machine's reading can be checked.

earnings_text.text: Q2 2026 (reported late July 2026): gross bookings $51.0 billion up 9%, revenue $7.4 billion up 8%, room nights 325 million up 5% (above the top of the outlook), adjusted EPS $2.54 up 15%, adjusted EBITDA $2.6 billion up 9%. Q3 outlook: room nights up 3 to 5%, revenue up 4 to 6%. Full year: high single digit revenue growth, low to mid teens EPS growth. Q1 2026 also beat with the same AI overhang on the stock.

read.headline: Q2 2026 beat on every metric the note lists — room nights came in above the top of the outlook and adjusted EPS rose 15% — while the Q3 room-night outlook of 3 to 5% sits below the 5% just delivered and the stock is down about 24% on the year.

guidance.detail: Q3 room nights guided up 3 to 5% and revenue up 4 to 6%. The note does not label this as raised, cut or maintained and gives no prior Q3 outlook to compare against, so the direction of any revision cannot be determined from the file. Read against the quarter just reported (room nights up 5%, revenue up 8%), both ranges sit at or below the delivered growth rates.
guidance.quote: Q3 outlook: room nights up 3 to 5%, revenue up 4 to 6%.

guidance.what: Full year 2026 revenue and adjusted EPS growth
guidance.detail: Full year framed as high single digit revenue growth and low to mid teens EPS growth. The note gives no earlier version of this full-year outlook, so whether it was raised, cut or maintained is not determinable from the file.
guidance.quote: Full year: high single digit revenue growth, low to mid teens EPS growth.

guidance.what: Full year adjusted EPS growth, as carried into the valuation section
guidance.detail: The valuation section restates the same low-to-mid-teens EPS growth guide and pairs it with the current multiple. The note's own three-year scenarios assume 12% EPS growth, which is the author's assumption, not a company figure.

guidance.what: Capital returns: buyback pace, dividend, remaining authorization
guidance.detail: $3.7 billion of buybacks in a single quarter, a $0.42 dividend, and $14.5 billion of authorization remaining. The note presents these as reported facts, not as a forward commitment, and states no target buyback pace. The separate claim that buybacks shrink the share count 4 to 5% a year appears in the valuation section as the note author's own modelling, not as company guidance.
guidance.quote: The company returned $3.7 billion through buybacks in a single quarter plus a $0.42 dividend, with $14.5 billion of authorization remaining.

tone.assessment: Management tone cannot be assessed from this note — it contains no quotes from the call or the release and no characterization of how management spoke. What the file conveys is the note author's tone: confident on the business, dismissive of the sentiment driving the stock. It frames the quarter as a beat (room nights above the top of the outlook, Q1 'also beat') and explicitly opposes results against sentiment, then closes with a buy and a 4 of 5 conviction score.
tone.evidence: The stock is down about 24% this year on AI agent fears while the business posted record results.
tone.confidence: low — and not higher because the note is a secondhand summary. It lists a Q2 2026 call transcript among its sources but reproduces no management language, no Q&A exchange, and no prepared-remarks detail. Any read of management tone would be inferred from an analyst's paraphrase rather than observed.

dodged.topic: The actual take rate realized in the reported quarter
dodged.reasoning: The Q2 paragraph lists gross bookings, revenue, room nights, adjusted EPS and adjusted EBITDA, but no take rate. The only two places 'take rate' appears in the file are the bear case (a hypothetical two-point compression) and the thesis killers (a 100 bps threshold). So the single metric the note treats as the thesis killer is the one it never reports a value for. Whether management disclosed it and the note omitted it, or management never gave it, cannot be told from this file.

dodged.topic: Any company response to the AI-disintermediation argument
dodged.reasoning: The note names the overhang once, in the Q2/Q1 paragraph, and calls it 'AI agent fears' in the why-it-is-on-the-list section, then lays out the bear case in full. Nothing in the file records what the company said about it. The only counter-evidence offered is a third-party market event from March 2026, which the note itself downgrades to evidence rather than proof.

dodged.topic: Cost and margin drivers behind the quarter
dodged.reasoning: Revenue is up 8% and adjusted EBITDA up 9% in the same quarter, so margin moved, but no expense line, marketing spend, or margin bridge appears anywhere in the file. The word 'marketing' does not occur in the note at all.

dodged.topic: Sizing of the Middle East demand impact and any regional split
dodged.reasoning: The conflict is asserted to be hurting travel demand in the bear case but is never quantified, and no regional breakdown of bookings or room nights appears. The note names Europe and Asia only as supply strengths in the business-quality section. It is not determinable whether this was raised with management at all.

dodged.topic: How the Q3 guide reconciles with the full-year guide
dodged.reasoning: Q3 revenue is guided up 4 to 6% while the full year is framed as high single digit revenue growth. The note presents both figures side by side without addressing the implied Q4 step-up. Whether management explained that bridge is not in the file.

read.market_reaction: Not stated for this print. The note gives no share-price move on or after the Q2 2026 report. The only price move it attaches to a date is a rise of 8% in March 2026 on the OpenAI checkout news, which is unrelated to this quarter. The surrounding context it does give is positional, not reactive: down about 24% this year, -12% from the 52 week high, -14% from the all time high, and a 2026-09-04 price of 195.13 recorded roughly six weeks after the report. One indirect hint sits outside the note's prose — the Investing.com source URL contains the slug "shares-jump" — but the note's body never states a post-earnings move, so I am not treating that as a reported fact.
not_determinable: Whether any guidance was raised, cut, maintained or withdrawn. The note carries no prior-period guidance ranges. Its one comparative statement is that Q2 room nights came in 'above the top of the outlook' without ever saying what that outlook was.
The take rate or commission rate actually realized in Q2 2026. The 15% figure appears only inside the bear-case argument, and the 100 bps figure only as a thesis-killer threshold.
Guidance in absolute dollars. Every forward figure in the note is a growth rate or a range of growth rates; there is no dollar EPS, revenue or bookings guide for Q3 or the full year.

Any FY2027 or multi-year company guidance. The three-year outcomes (about $200 bear, about $310 base, about $380 bull) are the note author's scenario math built on an assumed 12% EPS growth rate, not company figures.
The share-price reaction to the Q2 print itself (see market_reaction).
Anything management actually said. The note lists a Q2 2026 call transcript among its sources but reproduces no quote, no Q&A, and no prepared remarks.

Any breakdown by brand or region. Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, Kayak and OpenTable are named once in the business description and never again; no bookings, revenue or room nights are split by brand or geography.

Marketing spend and channel economics. The note asserts the company has 'the most direct traffic' but gives no direct-versus-paid mix, no performance-marketing spend, and no customer-acquisition figures. Nothing in the file describes a loyalty programme or its penetration.

Quarter-end share count and the forward buyback pace. The most recent share figure in the file is the FY2025 diluted count of 816 million; the $3.7 billion of buybacks is described as a single quarter with no statement that the pace continues.
Gross margin in any year. The financial table shows n/a for all four fiscal years.
Any history before FY2022. The note states plainly that four fiscal years is all the source provides, so multi-cycle comparisons are not possible from this file.

Estimate-revision detail beyond one line. The file contains only 'Next fiscal year EPS estimate moved +0.5% in 90 days' — no 30-day figure, no count of analysts revising up versus down, no dispersion, and no per-analyst data. Any more precise revision statistics would have to come from a source outside this note.

Valuation inputs beyond the rounded screen figures. The file gives forward P/E 15.8, a 29.5 four-year median and EV/EBITDA 14.4, and nothing more precise; there is also no Expedia comparable, which the note flags as not in the screen.
Year-ago quarterly bases. Growth rates are given, but no prior-year quarterly room nights, bookings or EPS appear, so the Q3 3 to 5% guide cannot be tested against comparison difficulty.

Position sizing, portfolio weight, or any trade record. The note ends at a buy zone of $178 to $205 and a conviction of 4 of 5. It contains no position size, no dollar or percentage target, no entry log and no cross-reference to any journal or trade record — the word 'journal' does not occur in the file. Any such figures would come from a different document.
The order and dates of the last two reports beyond what is stated. Q2 2026 is dated only as 'late July 2026' and Q1 2026 carries no date or figures at all.

Whether the Q2 beat was driven by volume, price or mix. Room nights up 5% against gross bookings up 9% implies a higher average booking value, but the note never states an ADR, a currency effect, or a mix explanation.

thesis.why_on_the_list: Compounder bucket, rank 13. ROIC 43%, 34% free cash flow margin, share count down 19% over the window. Forward P/E 15.8 vs a 29.5 median. The stock is down about 24% this year on AI agent fears while the business posted record results.
thesis.business_quality: Two sided network: the most hotel supply, especially in Europe and Asia, and the most direct traffic. Payments platform handles 100 plus methods and 50 plus currencies. The company returned $3.7 billion through buybacks in a single quarter plus a $0.42 dividend, with $14.5 billion of authorization remaining. Cash $17.2 billion against $20.2 billion of debt.
thesis.verdict: Buy now, September tranche. Buy zone $178 to $205. Conviction 4 of 5.

logged.thesis: Record bookings, room nights up 5%, EPS up 15%, at 15.8x forward against a 29.5x median. Buybacks of $3.7 billion a quarter shrink the count 4 to 5% a year. The AI agent fear is priced as certainty.
logged.wrong_if: Two quarters of negative room nights, take rate down 100 basis points, or a close under $150.

risks.bear_case: AI agents will talk directly to hotel systems and a 15% commission will not survive that. Growth is already slowing to mid single digits in room nights, the Middle East conflict is hurting travel demand, and Google keeps pushing its own hotel booking. If the take rate compresses by even two points, earnings fall 15%.
killers: two consecutive quarters of negative room nights, take rate falling more than 100 basis points year over year, or buybacks pausing

wrong_if.text: Two quarters of negative room nights, take rate down 100 basis points, or a close under $150.

multiples.label: Forward P/E
multiples.basis_note: The two sides are not the same multiple. The left is a forward P/E, the Street's estimate of next year's earnings. The median on the right is trailing: the price at each fiscal year end divided by that year's reported diluted EPS. Where earnings are expected to grow, forward is mechanically lower than trailing, so this column reads cheap by construction.

multiples.label: EV/EBITDA
multiples.basis_note: Both sides are trailing, so this comparison is like for like.

own_history.caveat: The median is taken at 4 fiscal year ends, so it is a 4-point median. That is a thin basis for 'cheap against its own history' and it says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved.
own_history.basis_warning: Read the P/E row with care. Across the 136 names that carry both comparisons, 85% print a negative 'vs median' on forward P/E with a median of -29%, against 50% and 0.0% on EV/EBITDA where both sides are trailing. That gap is the basis mismatch, not 136 companies being cheap. It is also correlated with growth: faster-growing names look cheaper here (rank correlation -0.28 against revenue CAGR, versus -0.15 for EV/EBITDA), because their forward earnings are further above their trailing ones. The score weights the like-for-like EV/EBITDA comparison more heavily for exactly this reason.

drawdown.caveat: The all-time high is the highest closing price; the 52-week high is an intraday high. They are not on the same basis, and the drawdown from the all-time high is therefore understated.

price_basis.note: The drawdowns and the multiple-versus-median above were computed inside the price screen from its own last close, which is not quite the price shown at the top of this page: the two come from different passes of the pipeline and differ by a fraction of a percent. Neither is wrong; they are just not the same number.

peer_set.label: Consumer Cyclical
peer_set.caveat: Not enough names in its industry to compare against, so this is against 24 others in Consumer Cyclical. A sector holds businesses that are not really comparable, so read the percentile loosely.

peers.verdict: priced below where its quality sits
peers.reasoning: It is mid-pack on price and the best quartile on quality, 45 points apart: the market is pricing it below where its measured characteristics rank among its peers. That gap is the observation. Whether it is an opportunity depends entirely on something outside these numbers.
peers.why: The own-history comparison above says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved. This asks a different question: where does this name sit among its peers on price, and where does it sit among them on the things a price is supposed to reflect.

written_view.text: At $195 and 15.8x forward with full year adjusted EPS growth guided to low to mid teens. Peers: Airbnb 30x, Expedia not in the screen. Three year view with 12% EPS growth: bear 13x on stalled growth is about $200, flat; base 18x is about $310; bull 22x is about $380. Buybacks shrink the count 4 to 5% a year, which does much of the compounding on its own.

score.caveat: A percentile against 150 names on one date. It has not been backtested; see the positioning page for why not.
